body:
## Analysis, and a recommendation that is none of the three options above

Investigated properly. Four new facts change the decision, and one claim in the issue body above is **wrong** — correcting that first.

### ❌ Correction: Studio's inspector is not derived from the props schema

The body says *"Studio's inspector cannot offer the prop, because it derives fields from the props schema."* That is not how it works. `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/block-config.ts:216` is a **hand-written** table, and its own header says so: *"Keep each field `name` aligned with the property name the corresponding renderer reads."* For `element:button` it lists `label`, `variant`, `size`, `icon` — and no `action`.

So declaring the prop in the spec buys validation and discoverability, but **not** an inspector field; that is a separate hand edit either way. `block-config.ts` is itself a fourth hand-maintained shadow of the spec's block props, which is the same disease #2901 catalogued — worth its own cleanup, and it means "declare the prop" does not by itself make the button authorable in Studio.

### 1. This is live in production, not a curiosity

`cloud` main, `packages/service-tenant/src/pages/`:

| Site | Shape |
|---|---|
| `pricing.page.ts:42` | `const goToEnvironments = { type: 'navigation', to: ENVIRONMENTS_ROUTE }` |
| `welcome.page.ts:66` | `const go = (to) => ({ type: 'navigation', to })` — used 4× |
| `billing-cancel.page.ts:66, :76` | `{ type: 'navigation', to: … }` |
| `billing-success.page.ts:74` | `{ type: 'navigation', to: … }` |

Five declaration sites, ~9 rendered buttons, four pages — the billing and pricing funnel. Every one is cast `as any`, which is how they get past the type system today.

**They use only `type` and `to`.** No `replace`, no `newTab`, no `external`, no `navigate`. That matters: folding `navigation` onto `url` loses nothing anyone actually writes.

### 2. The renderer accepts three action dialects simultaneously

`packages/components/src/renderers/basic/elements.tsx:212-240` forwards, verbatim:

```
type | actionType,  name, label, description, target, openIn, endpoint,
method, navigate, to, opensInNewTab, confirmText, successMessage,
errorMessage, refreshAfter, params → {params | actionParams}
```

That is `ActionSchema`'s own field set (**`actionType`** is the dashboard-widget spelling, **`navigate`/`to`** the navigation spelling) — three vocabularies for one concept, in one 25-line callback. Of those, `ActionSchema` declares all but **`endpoint`, `navigate`, `to`, `replace`**.

### 3. An undeclared prop is *stripped*, not ignored — a loaded gun

```
ElementButtonPropsSchema.safeParse({ label: 'Go', action: { type: 'navigation', to: '/x' } })
→ success: true, data: { label: 'Go', variant: 'primary', size: 'medium', iconPosition: 'left', … }
```

No `action`. It is a non-strict `z.object`, so Zod drops the unknown key.

Harmless **today**, because page block `properties` are `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` (`page.zod.ts:86`) and this schema never runs on a real page save. But the moment anyone tightens `properties` to validate against `COMPONENT_PROPS_SCHEMAS` — an obvious future hardening — **every cloud button silently loses its action at save**, with a green parse. Declaring the prop defuses that; nothing else does.

### 4. Two constraints that kill the obvious fixes

**`ActionSchema` requires `name` and `label`.** Verified:

```
{type:'url', target:'/x'}                → name: required, label: required
{name, type, target}                     → label: required
{name, label, type, target}              → OK
```

A page button already has `properties.label`. `action: ActionSchema` would force the author to write the label **twice** and invent a `name` for something that is not a reusable named action. Option 1 as written is not ergonomic.

**The `lazySchema` proxy does not forward object-structural methods.** Verified against 17.0.0-rc.0:

| Call | Result |
|---|---|
| `ChartTypeSchema.extract([...])`, `.options` | ✅ works (enum proxy) |
| `ActionSchema.pick(...)` | ❌ *not a function* |
| `ActionSchema.omit(...)` / `.extend(...)` / `.shape` | ❌ not available |

So `action: ActionSchema.pick({ … the 16 fields the renderer honours … })` — the derivation I would have wanted — **is not expressible**. Enum subsetting is available (that is how objectstack#4070 derived `ListChartConfigSchema.chartType`); object subsetting is not.

## Recommendation

**Declare the prop against a new `InlineActionSchema`, and treat `navigation`/`to` as normalizing aliases of `url`/`target` with a scheduled removal — not as new members.**

Splitting the decision the issue conflated:

- **D1 — declare `action`?** Unambiguously yes. It is live in production, it feeds a real dispatcher, it is the only thing making a standalone-page button interactive, and leaving it undeclared keeps the silent-strip gun loaded. This is the part that closes this issue.
- **D2 — pointing at what?** None of the three options above is right:

| Option | Verdict |
|---|---|
| 1. `action: ActionSchema` | Right instinct, wrong shape — requires a duplicate `label` and an invented `name`, and cannot be narrowed via `.pick` |
| 2. own narrow schema naming `navigation` + `to` | Blesses a **fourth** action-type vocabulary permanently (after `ActionType`, the now-unified `WidgetActionType`, and `types/src/api-types.ts`'s 7-member union). Rejected for the reason this issue exists |
| 3. promote `navigation` into `ActionType` | Does not close this issue at all — names the *type*, leaves the *prop* undeclared and `to` homeless. Half a fix, and a permanent synonym |

### Concretely

**Stage A — framework, no breakage.** Add `InlineActionSchema` to `action.zod.ts`: the ~16 fields the ElementButton renderer actually honours, with `name`/`label` **optional** (an inline action has no registry identity, and the button supplies its own label). Declare `ElementButtonPropsSchema.action = InlineActionSchema.optional()`. Accept `navigation` and `to` as `z.preprocess` aliases folding to `url`/`target` — the `VIEW_FILTER_OPERATOR_ALIASES` pattern, a bridge with a defined end state rather than a new enum member. Since `.pick` is unavailable, `InlineActionSchema` will restate its fields; pin it to `ActionSchema` with a parity test (the same substitute `filter-view-operator-parity.test.ts` uses for the `data/`↔`ui/` layering constraint) so the two cannot drift.

Decide `endpoint` here too: the renderer forwards it and `ActionSchema` does not declare it — either it joins the inline schema or objectui stops forwarding it.

**Stage B — cloud.** Rewrite the five sites to `{ type: 'url', target: … }` and drop the `as any`. Note the graft from objectstack#4107 does **not** help here: those pages are code-defined `*.page.ts`, not `saveMeta`-persisted, so nothing canonicalizes them automatically.

**Stage C — framework, next major.** `retiredKey`-tombstone `to`; drop the `navigation` alias. By then `executeUrl`'s richer semantics (`${param.X}`/`${ctx.X}` interpolation, `apiBase` promotion for `/api/…` paths, popup-blocker-safe `openIn`) are what page buttons get, instead of `executeNavigation`'s strictly weaker behaviour.

**Also, separately:** add `action` to `block-config.ts`'s `element:button` entry, or the Studio inspector still cannot author it — and consider deriving that table from `COMPONENT_PROPS_SCHEMAS` rather than hand-keeping it.

### Ordering

Framework first, then cloud (cloud links `@objectstack/*` to framework `main`). Stage A adds no export cloud must import, so cloud can lag safely — the alias keeps its current pages valid throughout. Nothing in Stage A rejects anything that parses today, so it carries no migration.

Refs objectstack-ai/objectstack#4070 (where promoting `navigation` bare was considered and declined), objectstack-ai/objectstack#4107, #2945

## Stage A implemented — objectstack-ai/objectstack#4135, and a correction to my own diagnosis

### Correction: `.pick` is unavailable because of the refine chain, not the `lazySchema` proxy

My analysis above blamed the proxy. Wrong. Reading `shared/lazy-schema.ts`, the proxy's `get` handler forwards **everything** — `real[prop]`, binding functions — which is exactly why `ChartTypeSchema.extract([…])` works (that one wraps a bare `z.enum`).

The actual cause is that `ActionSchema` is `z.object(…).refine(…).refine(…)`. `.pick()` is a `ZodObject` method, and two refinement wrappers stand between it and the export. Same observable symptom, different fix — and the difference matters, because it means subsetting **is** achievable by splitting the object half out, which the proxy story would have ruled out.

So the implementation is better than what I proposed:

```ts
const actionObject = () => z.object({ …47 fields… });
export const ActionSchema       = lazySchema(() => actionObject().refine(…).refine(…)…);
export const InlineActionSchema = lazySchema(() => z.preprocess(normalizeInlineAction,
  actionObject().pick({ …12 fields… }).partial({ name: true, label: true }).refine(…)));
```

**Real derivation — no parity test needed.** I recommended a parity test above as a substitute for the derivation I thought was impossible; it isn't needed, because the field definitions are now literally the same objects. A factory rather than a module-scope const so `lazySchema`'s deferral survives (fields built on first use of whichever schema is touched, not at module load).

### What shipped in Stage A

- `InlineActionSchema` — the twelve fields `element:button` actually forwards, `name`/`label` optional, `target`-required refinement inherited, registry-only concerns excluded.
- `ElementButtonPropsSchema.action = InlineActionSchema.optional()` — the prop is declared, so it stops being silently stripped.
- `normalizeInlineAction` — folds `type:'navigation'` → `'url'` and `to` → `target` on parse. cloud's five sites keep validating unchanged; output is always canonical.
- 16 tests, including the derivation asserted from both directions and the fold pinned against the literal shape cloud writes. Full spec suite 7038/271 green, `tsc` clean, all twelve `check:*` gates pass, zero removals from any generated surface.

### Remaining, in order

1. **Stage B — cloud:** rewrite the five `service-tenant` sites to `{ type: 'url', target }`, drop the `as any`. Waiting on Stage A to merge (cloud links `@objectstack/*` to framework `main`).
2. **objectui — `block-config.ts`:** add an `action` field to the `element:button` entry, or Studio still cannot author it. Independent of Stage A; the table is hand-written.
3. **Stage C — next major:** `retiredKey`-tombstone `to`, drop the `navigation` alias.

One correction to the issue body's framing while I am here: the body says the prop being undeclared means "no validation … a typo in `action.type` or a missing `to` fails silently at click time rather than at save". That is right in direction but was understated — the prop was not merely unvalidated, it was **deleted** from the parse output. That is now in the analysis above with the executed evidence.

## Stages A and B done, plus the Studio half — this issue is closed out

| Stage | Repo | PR |
|---|---|---|
| A — `InlineActionSchema`, prop declared, aliases fold | framework | objectstack-ai/objectstack#4135 ✅ |
| B — migrate the five producers to `url` + `target` | cloud | objectstack-ai/cloud#926 ✅ |
| Studio — a new button can be *given* an action | objectui | #3028 ✅ |

### Two corrections to my own analysis in this thread

**1. `.pick` was blocked by the refine chain, not the `lazySchema` proxy.** The proxy forwards everything. `ActionSchema` is `z.object(…).refine(…).refine(…)`, and `.pick()` is a `ZodObject` method. Splitting the object half into a factory made real derivation possible, so the parity test I proposed as a substitute was not needed — the field definitions are literally the same objects now.

**2. "Studio cannot author it" was half right.** The "Advanced" section *can* edit an `action` that source authored; what it cannot do is **add** one, because it enumerates `Object.keys(blockProps)` — the keys the block already has. So a button dragged from the palette had no path to becoming interactive. #3028 adds a `json` field kind (the same editor Advanced uses, reachable for a property that does not exist yet) and an `action` field with the canonical shape as its placeholder.

**3. The Stage A PR body said Stage B would "drop the `as any`".** It does not, and should not: those casts are for `children` on `page:section`, which the strict `PageComponent` type does not model. The comment above each one says so. Nothing to do with the action shape.

### What remains — Stage C, next major

`retiredKey`-tombstone `to` and drop the `navigation` alias from `normalizeInlineAction`. Both producers are migrated now, so the bridge has nothing left to carry — but removing it is a breaking parse change, so it waits for a major.

Worth noting for whoever does it: objectui's `ElementButtonRenderer` still forwards `actionType`, `endpoint`, `navigate` and `description` to the runner, none of which `InlineActionSchema` declares. `actionType` is the dashboard-widget spelling, `endpoint` is a third spelling of `target` (`executeAPI` reads `action.api || action.endpoint || action.target`), and `description` is not on `ActionSchema` at all. They are dead for authored metadata now that the prop is declared, and trimming them is the natural companion to Stage C.

Closing — the declared-prop gap this issue was filed for is closed, and the remaining item is a scheduled removal rather than a defect.
